name: madIS
tagline: SQLite extended with Python functions and virtual tables, turning SQL into a data-processing workbench.
description: madIS is an extensible relational system from the MaDgIK lab at the University of Athens (Yannis Ioannidis' group), built on SQLite through the APSW wrapper. Its point is to do data work inside SQL: Python row, aggregate and virtual-table functions read files, URLs and other sources as tables, parse and transform text, and plug into a workflow engine, without importing data first. The authors compare it to Hive's SQL-plus-UDF style, minus the cluster, and say it handles tens of millions of rows on one machine; it also includes a multidimensional index to speed multi-constraint joins against external sources. Code dates from 2009-2013, and the GitHub repository sees only occasional updates, the latest in 2025.
statusNote: Academic system (University of Athens, c. 2009-2013); occasional commits since, most recently May 2025.

scale.notes: Single machine; tens of millions of rows per the authors.

strengths: Python row, aggregate and virtual-table functions callable directly from SQL
Query files and network sources as tables without importing them
Built-in workflow engine for multi-step transformations
Inherits SQLite's reliability and zero-administration footprint
weaknesses: Small academic codebase with sparse, aging documentation
Python UDF overhead on very large scans
useCases: Text and data wrangling pipelines expressed in SQL
Prototyping new operators or indexes for database research
Ad-hoc analysis joining local files with remote sources
